claims.text: A predictive model integrating HEA compositional descriptors with microstructural features can identify low-phonon-thermal-conductivity materials more accurately than conventional approaches.
Explicit representation of atomic-level disorder and defect densities captures the complex phonon-scattering mechanisms inherent in HEAs.
Uniform processing conditions ensure homogeneous atomic disorder in single-phase equiatomic HEAs.
A multivariate model can use compositional and microstructural descriptors to compute phonon-scattering rates.
High configurational entropy produces uniform atomic-scale disorder with minimal microsegregation in the HEAs within the proposed applicability domain.
Phonon transport typically dominates HEA thermal transport near or below room temperature.
Uniform atomic-level disorder, point defects, and mass fluctuations enhance phonon scattering.
Enhanced phonon scattering caused by disorder, point defects, and mass fluctuations lowers thermal conductivity.
Capturing atomic arrangement and defect density allows the model to correlate phonon-scattering strength with thermal conductivity more accurately.
Conventional compositional-averaging methods can overlook complex interactions relevant to low thermal conductivity.
The proposed model will achieve at least a 20% improvement in prediction accuracy relative to standard methods when validated against measurements.
Conventional approaches rely primarily on average compositional parameters without detailed microstructural integration.
Conventional approaches have higher prediction errors for low-thermal-conductivity HEAs.
The model will be less effective for HEAs with significant microsegregation or secondary-phase formation.
The model will be less effective at temperatures where electronic contributions to thermal conductivity become significant.
Time-domain thermoreflectance can provide the phonon thermal-conductivity measurements required for the proposed comparison.
Failure to achieve more than a 20% accuracy improvement over conventional methods is defined as a falsifying outcome.
A measured-versus-predicted thermal-conductivity discrepancy exceeding 10% in confirmed homogeneous samples is defined as a falsifying outcome.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome specifies at least a 20% improvement, which includes exactly 20%, whereas the falsification rule requires more than 20% and would therefore treat exactly 20% as failure.
